leftEvidence.title: All tribes gather to make David king

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Armed divisions from every tribe come to Hebron with undivided purpose, and Israel supplies food for three days of joy.
points.right: Hiram builds David a house, David recognizes established kingship, more children are named, and two inquiries lead to victories and spreading fame.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places the accession becomes a whole-Israel assembly with material abundance inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places house, family, repeated guidance, and international fear are joined inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Chronicles 12:23–40 and 1 Chronicles 14:1–17 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Household and Philistine victories are retold

payload.tension: 1 Chronicles 12:23–40 foregrounds the accession becomes a whole-Israel assembly with material abundance; 1 Chronicles 14:1–17 foregrounds house, family, repeated guidance, and international fear are joined. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
